chunks: And by his chain, from Al-Asam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a man came to him and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, is your father visited?
He said: Yes, and prayer is established near him, and prayer is established behind him, and one does not precede him.
He said: What is the reward for the one who visits him? He said: Paradise, if he believes in his Imamate.
He said: What is the reward for the one who neglects it out of preference? He said: Regret on the Day of Regret.
He said: What is the reward for the one who stays near him? He said: Every day is equal to a thousand months.

He said: What is the reward for the one who spends while traveling to him and the one who spends while at his grave? He said: One Dirham is equal to a thousand Dirhams. And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمُ بِأَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ: One Dirham equals a thousand Dirhams (reward multiplier)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and rulings for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the unique spiritual status of Imam Al-Hasan (a.s.) as a distinct locus of worship, where prayer behind his grave signifies following his Imamate rather than mere veneration. It underscores the Shia principle of 'tawassul' through the Ahl al-Bayt, linking material charity during ziyarah to multiplied divine rewards, thereby elevating the physical act of visiting into a comprehensive spiritual economy of faith and devotion.
